name: Textarea
description: Collects multi-line text; grows with its text from minRows to maxRows, then scrolls.

minRows.description: Rows shown when empty; the field grows from here as text is added

maxRows.description: Rows the field grows to before it scrolls. Omit to grow without limit

resize.description: Whether the person can drag the height. Width never resizes: it would break the column measure

size.description: Type size, inset and one-row height on the shared control ladder

invalid.description: The danger edge and aria-invalid; say why in a Field.Error

disabled.description: Dims the field and blocks input

readOnly.description: Shows the text on a dashed edge without letting it change

maxLength.description: The most characters allowed. Setting it shows a counter under the field

onValueChange.description: Called with the new value on every change

required.description: Marks the field required for form validation

when: Free-form text input that may span multiple lines
whenNot: A chat composer with a toolbar (use Prompt)
guidelines: Wrap in a Field for the label, description and error
Set minRows to the expected answer length and maxRows where the layout has a ceiling
Placeholder shows an example, not the label
maxLength shows the counter; past the limit it says so in words
Use resize="none" only when the layout truly cannot flex
accessibility: Field.Label names the textarea and Field.Description describes it
Field.Error is announced when it appears
Error text says what to fix, not just that it failed

examples.name: Default
examples.description: Three rows that grow with the text.
examples.code:
<Field>
  <Field.Label>Description</Field.Label>
  <Textarea placeholder="What does this change do, and why?" />
  <Field.Description>Reviewers read this first.</Field.Description>
</Field>

examples.name: With counter
examples.description: maxLength shows a live count under the field.
examples.code:
<Field>
  <Field.Label>Bio</Field.Label>
  <Textarea
    maxLength={200}
    defaultValue="Design engineer on the checkout team. I look after our tokens and the standards every screen is checked against."
  />
  <Field.Description>Shown on your profile.</Field.Description>
</Field>

examples.name: Invalid
examples.description: The danger edge with the reason under the field.
examples.code:
<Field invalid>
  <Field.Label>Reason for the exception</Field.Label>
  <Textarea placeholder="Why does this screen need a raw value?" />
  <Field.Error match>Add a reason so reviewers can approve the exception.</Field.Error>
</Field>

examples.name: Grow to a ceiling
examples.description: Starts at one row, grows to six, then scrolls.
examples.code:
<Field>
  <Field.Label>Notes</Field.Label>
  <Textarea
    minRows={1}
    maxRows={6}
    defaultValue={'Checkout: three raw colours\nCart: one spacing value\nHeader: icon button without a label'}
  />
</Field>

examples.name: Sizes
examples.description: Four steps on the control ladder.
examples.code:
<Stack gap="sm">
  <Textarea aria-label="Extra small" placeholder="Extra small" size="xs" minRows={1} />
  <Textarea aria-label="Small" placeholder="Small" size="sm" minRows={1} />
  <Textarea aria-label="Medium" placeholder="Medium" size="md" minRows={1} />
  <Textarea aria-label="Large" placeholder="Large" size="lg" minRows={1} />
</Stack>

examples.name: Fixed height
examples.code:
<Field>
  <Field.Label>Release notes</Field.Label>
  <Textarea
    resize="none"
    defaultValue="Buttons, inputs and selects now share one control height ladder, so a row of mixed controls lines up without overrides."
  />
</Field>

relations.note: Field supplies the label, description and error
Use Prompt for a chat composer

propsSummary: minRows / maxRows: grows with its text between them, then scrolls
invalid: boolean - danger edge plus aria-invalid; pair with Field.Error
maxLength: number - shows the counter automatically
onValueChange: (value: string) => void; onChange stays the native event
Label, description and error come from Field parts, never from Textarea props
...native textarea attributes are supported (readOnly, autoComplete, onKeyDown, etc.)
